pathway.title: Skeena Resources Ltd — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Skeena has no revenue and reports no EBITDA, so every earnings-based measure is Not supplied and the credit view rests on funding and project delivery [CP-1, financial base; Not calculable]. At June 30, 2026 the company held CAD 134,808 thousand of unrestricted cash and CAD 500,853 thousand of restricted cash, with CAD 316,513 thousand of undiscounted financial liabilities and commitments due within one year; the restricted balance is what makes the near-term picture covered, and its release conditions are not supplied [CP-1, liquidity and maturity table; CP-1A, transaction summary].

The April 10, 2026 notes offering is the pivot of the credit. It replaced the terminated US$350,000,000 term loan, funded the Gold Stream buy-down of US$184,000,000 and placed an interest reserve and a construction disbursement account in restricted cash. The notes carry 8.50% interest, mature on April 1, 2031 and are carried at CAD 1,055,969 thousand net of an embedded derivative asset, or CAD 1,082,552 thousand gross; their trading value implies a fair value of CAD 1,119,655 thousand, which exceeds both figures [CP-1, debt and financing instruments]. The company says proceeds should fund capital needs through commencement of commercial production in 2027 only if the conditions precedent are met; that is management language and the conditions are not supplied [CP-1A, transaction summary; Management Language].

Other claims sit beside the notes. The Gold Stream is a derivative liability of CAD 209,286 thousand and ranks pari passu with the notes; the two royalty liabilities are CAD 78,709 thousand and CAD 136,009 thousand; lease liabilities are CAD 66,483 thousand; and the closure and reclamation provision rose to CAD 104,777 thousand from CAD 46,227 thousand at December 31, 2025 [CP-1, claims outside the debt figure]. Total liabilities of CAD 1,746,295 thousand exceed shareholders' equity of CAD 170,801 thousand. A surety bond provides reclamation security, with collateral of unstated amount; this corrects the earlier financial base statement that none was found [CP-1A, correction].

The business is concentrated in one project. Management says Eskay Creek is fully permitted and expects commercial production in 2027, but those are management statements and the retained filings still list permit challenges as a risk [CP-1A, company and operating model; Management Language]. Documented issuer behaviour is equity-funded and supportive of funding, with bought deals in February 2025 and October 2025, and no creditor-adverse action is documented; no sponsor or controlling holder is identified [CP-1A, ownership and issuer behaviour].

runs.text: Strengths. Skeena has pre-funded its build: restricted cash of CAD 500,853 thousand, held for construction and interest, sits beside unrestricted cash of CAD 134,808 thousand, and both together of CAD 635,661 thousand exceed the CAD 316,513 thousand of undiscounted obligations due within one year [CP-1; Analyst Interpretation, because release of restricted funds is conditional]. The debt is a single fixed-rate bullet maturing on April 1, 2031 with no maturity inside the construction window other than interest, and the interest reserve covers three semi-annual payments [CP-1, debt and financing instruments; Documentary Fact]. The buy-down cut the Gold Stream from 10.55% to 3.52% of payable gold, reducing the stream's claim on future output [CP-1A, Gold Stream; Documentary Fact]. Equity markets were open to the company in 2025 and the company has documented no debt-funded distributions [CP-1A, ownership and issuer behaviour; Documentary Fact]. The notes' trading value exceeds their carrying amount, which is consistent with, but does not prove, market acceptance of the credit [CP-1; Analyst Interpretation].

Weaknesses. Skeena has no revenue, no EBITDA and no operating cash flow: six-month operating cash outflow was CAD 30,235 thousand and additions to mineral property, plant and equipment were CAD 203,600 thousand, so the build depends on financing already raised [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. Cost to complete, project budget and schedule are not supplied, so adequacy of the CAD 500,853 thousand of restricted cash cannot be tested [CP-1A; Insufficient Information]. Claims beside the notes are large relative to the equity base: the Gold Stream, two royalty liabilities, leases and the closure provision, plus a new 1% royalty and an option that could issue shares [CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. The company holds US dollar debt and restricted cash while reporting in Canadian dollars, recorded a foreign exchange loss of CAD 17,684 thousand in the six months and does not hedge [CP-1; Documentary Fact]. Single-asset concentration means a permit, construction or metallurgical event affects the whole credit [CP-1A; Analyst Interpretation]. If the Gold Stream completion test is not met by September 30, 2027 the stream percentage steps up from 3.52% [CP-1A; Documentary Fact]. Whether the Gold Stream covenants (debt service coverage and a cash minimum) still apply after the buy-down is Not supplied [CP-1; Insufficient Information].

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The principal new debt issue is the offering of US$750,000,000 aggregate principal amount of Senior Secured Notes, completed on April 10, 2026 and stated in the statements as 1,036,761 (CAD thousands) (Q2 FS page:12). The notes bear interest at 8.50% per annum payable semi-annually, mature on April 1, 2031, are non-callable for the first two years, and are described as senior secured obligations ranking pari passu with the Gold Stream obligations and senior to all present and future subordinated indebtedness. Before April 1, 2028 the company may redeem some or all of the notes at 100% plus the greater of 1% and a make-whole premium of 50 basis points over the treasury yield, up to 10% at 103%, or up to 40% with net cash proceeds of equity offerings at 108.5%; from April 1, 2028 the redemption price is 104.25% until March 31, 2029, 102.125% until March 31, 2030 and 100% thereafter. A change of control triggers an offer at 101%, and excess proceeds from asset sales above a threshold must be used to offer to purchase the notes (Q2 FS page:12, page:13). Parties other than the issuer (initial purchasers, trustee, any guarantors and the security package) are Not supplied. The use of proceeds as stated in the statements was 254,352 (US$184,000,000) to repurchase 66.67% of the Gold Stream, 130,228 (US$94,208,000) to an interest reserve account representing three semi-annual interest payments, 552,940 (US$400,000,000) to support construction through a disbursement account, and 99,241 (US$71,792,000) for general and administrative expenses and issuance costs. By June 30, 2026, 199,176 (US$145,000,000) of the restricted proceeds had been released and restricted cash stood at 500,853, with cash and cash equivalents of 134,808 (CAD thousands). The company says the proceeds are expected to be sufficient to fund capital requirements through commencement of commercial production in 2027 only "As long as the Company meets the conditions precedent to the Senior Secured Notes", and that additional financing would be needed if funds cannot be released or are insufficient (Q2 FS page:4). The conditions precedent and release mechanics are not supplied.

The notes replaced the earlier funding plan. Under the June 24, 2024 agreements with Orion, the Project Financing Package consisted of private placements, a Gold Stream with a US$200,000,000 deposit and a US$350,000,000 Senior Secured Term Loan facility (Q3 2025 FS page:4; Q1 FS page:9, page:10). The deposit was fully received by December 31, 2025 and no draws were made on the term loan, which was terminated on April 10, 2026 (Q2 FS page:14). On March 31, 2026 the company entered into an amending agreement to exercise the buy-down option for US$184,000,000 and cancel the option to draw an additional deposit (Q1 FS page:11). The buy-down reduced the Stream Percentage by 66.67%, from 10.55% to 3.52% of payable gold. The earlier agreement priced the buy-down as the proportional deposit plus an imputed 18% internal rate of return and available for 12 months after the project completion date (Q3 2025 FS page:11); the 2026 early exercise was negotiated, and its pricing basis is not supplied. In the same half-year the company completed an agreement granting third parties a 1% NSR royalty on Eskay Creek and a right to elect an additional NSR royalty or shares, valued at 116,474 and 266,950 at initial recognition respectively (CAD thousands), with a 25,000 prepayment of royalty obligations in the second quarter (Q2 FS page:15, page:16). The equity component of the option, 108,575, was booked to reserves (Q2 FS page:2). Equity funding included a bought deal closed on February 26, 2025 for gross proceeds of 88,347 and another closed on October 8, 2025 for gross proceeds of 143,796 (CAD thousands) (Q3 2025 FS page:12, page:13).

The Q1 FS and the Q2 FS describe the construction account differently: the Q1 FS says the remaining proceeds "will be used to support the remaining construction at Eskay through a reimbursement account", while the Q2 FS says "through a disbursement account" (Q1 FS page:15; Q2 FS page:12). This is logged below as a wording difference and not reconciled. Terms of the Gold Stream covenants (debt service coverage of no less than 1.25:1 after the completion test and a minimum unrestricted cash of 25,000 after the term loan and additional deposit commitments end) were stated before the buy-down (Q1 FS page:10, page:11) and are not repeated in the Q2 FS; their current status is Not supplied.

fields.value: Skeena is a development-stage company with no revenue line in any retained statement, so the financial base is a funding and liquidity base, not an earnings base. At June 30, 2026 the company had completed the April 10, 2026 offering of US$750,000,000 Senior Secured Notes (stated as 1,036,761 CAD thousands at issue), used part of the proceeds to repurchase 66.67% of the Gold Stream, and placed the interest reserve and construction disbursement proceeds in restricted accounts. The consolidated balance sheet at that date shows unrestricted cash of 134,808, restricted cash of 500,853, long-term debt carrying value of 1,055,969 and total liabilities of 1,746,295 against shareholders' equity of 170,801 (CAD thousands). The net loss for the six months ended June 30, 2026 was 139,677, including a 41,736 fair value loss on the Gold Stream derivative and a 17,684 foreign exchange loss; operating cash outflow was 30,235 and additions to mineral property, plant and equipment were 203,600 for the same six months. Because earnings measures do not exist, the report's leverage and interest cover chart cells are Not supplied, and the funding picture is read from cash, restricted cash, the maturity table and the construction commitments. The limits are material: the statements are unaudited, FY2025 full-year flows and the audited notes are not in the pack, cash interest paid for the half-year is not stated, and neither the legal terms of the notes nor the cost to complete is supplied. Debt figures that involve US dollar balances move with exchange rates, and the company states that it does not use derivatives to reduce exposure to foreign exchange risk (Q2 FS, page:10).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The credit story is a single-asset, pre-revenue construction financing. Skeena states that it is "a mining company in the development stage focusing on the construction and development of the Eskay Creek project" (Q2 FS, page:4), and management says the project is "fully permitted and under construction" with "initial production and cash flow in the second quarter of 2027" (Aug 2026 release, page:1). Those timing and quality statements are management language, not audited facts. The financing was rebuilt in the first half of 2026. The June 2024 package with Orion (private placements, a Gold Stream and a US$350,000,000 Senior Secured Term Loan) was replaced on April 10, 2026 by an offering of US$750,000,000 Senior Secured Notes at 8.50% due April 1, 2031. Part of the proceeds repurchased 66.67% of the Gold Stream for US$184,000,000, part went to an interest reserve account covering three semi-annual interest payments, part to a construction disbursement account, and the remainder to general expenses and issuance costs. Creditors therefore sit alongside a reduced stream, new and existing NSR royalties, a growing closure obligation and unreleased restricted cash. The mechanics that matter are release conditions on the restricted accounts, completion-test timing for the Gold Stream percentage, and cost to complete, none of which can be tested from the retained documents. There is no sponsor and no controlling holder is identified. Documented issuer behaviour is equity-funded and transparent in its disclosure of financing events; no creditor-adverse action is documented. The notes' indenture, the Gold Stream and royalty agreements, the annual information form and the technical report are not in the pack, so legal capacity, security and guarantor structure are Insufficient Information. This view is a statement of business and transaction facts and their credit mechanics, not a view on credit quality or recovery.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The principal new debt issue is the offering of US$750,000,000 aggregate principal amount of Senior Secured Notes, completed on April 10, 2026 and stated in the statements as 1,036,761 (CAD thousands) (Q2 FS page:12). The notes bear interest at 8.50% per annum payable semi-annually, mature on April 1, 2031, are non-callable for the first two years, and are described as senior secured obligations ranking pari passu with the Gold Stream obligations and senior to all present and future subordinated indebtedness. Before April 1, 2028 the company may redeem some or all of the notes at 100% plus the greater of 1% and a make-whole premium of 50 basis points over the treasury yield, up to 10% at 103%, or up to 40% with net cash proceeds of equity offerings at 108.5%; from April 1, 2028 the redemption price is 104.25% until March 31, 2029, 102.125% until March 31, 2030 and 100% thereafter. A change of control triggers an offer at 101%, and excess proceeds from asset sales above a threshold must be used to offer to purchase the notes (Q2 FS page:12, page:13). Parties other than the issuer (initial purchasers, trustee, any guarantors and the security package) are Not supplied. The use of proceeds as stated in the statements was 254,352 (US$184,000,000) to repurchase 66.67% of the Gold Stream, 130,228 (US$94,208,000) to an interest reserve account representing three semi-annual interest payments, 552,940 (US$400,000,000) to support construction through a disbursement account, and 99,241 (US$71,792,000) for general and administrative expenses and issuance costs. By June 30, 2026, 199,176 (US$145,000,000) of the restricted proceeds had been released and restricted cash stood at 500,853, with cash and cash equivalents of 134,808 (CAD thousands). The company says the proceeds are expected to be sufficient to fund capital requirements through commencement of commercial production in 2027 only "As long as the Company meets the conditions precedent to the Senior Secured Notes", and that additional financing would be needed if funds cannot be released or are insufficient (Q2 FS page:4). The conditions precedent and release mechanics are not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The notes replaced the earlier funding plan. Under the June 24, 2024 agreements with Orion, the Project Financing Package consisted of private placements, a Gold Stream with a US$200,000,000 deposit and a US$350,000,000 Senior Secured Term Loan facility (Q3 2025 FS page:4; Q1 FS page:9, page:10). The deposit was fully received by December 31, 2025 and no draws were made on the term loan, which was terminated on April 10, 2026 (Q2 FS page:14). On March 31, 2026 the company entered into an amending agreement to exercise the buy-down option for US$184,000,000 and cancel the option to draw an additional deposit (Q1 FS page:11). The buy-down reduced the Stream Percentage by 66.67%, from 10.55% to 3.52% of payable gold. The earlier agreement priced the buy-down as the proportional deposit plus an imputed 18% internal rate of return and available for 12 months after the project completion date (Q3 2025 FS page:11); the 2026 early exercise was negotiated, and its pricing basis is not supplied. In the same half-year the company completed an agreement granting third parties a 1% NSR royalty on Eskay Creek and a right to elect an additional NSR royalty or shares, valued at 116,474 and 266,950 at initial recognition respectively (CAD thousands), with a 25,000 prepayment of royalty obligations in the second quarter (Q2 FS page:15, page:16). The equity component of the option, 108,575, was booked to reserves (Q2 FS page:2). Equity funding included a bought deal closed on February 26, 2025 for gross proceeds of 88,347 and another closed on October 8, 2025 for gross proceeds of 143,796 (CAD thousands) (Q3 2025 FS page:12, page:13).

This is logged below as a wording difference and not reconciled. Terms of the Gold Stream covenants (debt service coverage of no less than 1.25:1 after the completion test and a minimum unrestricted cash of 25,000 after the term loan and additional deposit commitments end) were stated before the buy-down (Q1 FS page:10, page:11) and are not repeated in the Q2 FS; their current status is Not supplied.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Skeena is a pre-revenue, single-asset construction credit that is funded for now but unproven, and the evidence supports a cautious, not an adverse, view. The strongest support is liquidity: CAD 134,808 thousand of unrestricted cash and CAD 500,853 thousand of restricted cash at June 30, 2026, a US$750,000,000 fixed-rate note due April 1, 2031 and an interest reserve covering three semi-annual payments. The weakest point is that no earnings or cost-to-complete figure exists, so leverage, cover and funding adequacy cannot be measured. The outcome turns on delivery of Eskay Creek and the September 30, 2027 completion test, on release of restricted cash, and on the notes' legal terms, which are not in the pack.

fields.value: Skeena has no revenue and reports no EBITDA, so every earnings-based measure is Not supplied and the credit view rests on funding and project delivery [CP-1, financial base; Not calculable]. At June 30, 2026 the company held CAD 134,808 thousand of unrestricted cash and CAD 500,853 thousand of restricted cash, with CAD 316,513 thousand of undiscounted financial liabilities and commitments due within one year; the restricted balance is what makes the near-term picture covered, and its release conditions are not supplied [CP-1, liquidity and maturity table; CP-1A, transaction summary].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The April 10, 2026 notes offering is the pivot of the credit. It replaced the terminated US$350,000,000 term loan, funded the Gold Stream buy-down of US$184,000,000 and placed an interest reserve and a construction disbursement account in restricted cash. The notes carry 8.50% interest, mature on April 1, 2031 and are carried at CAD 1,055,969 thousand net of an embedded derivative asset, or CAD 1,082,552 thousand gross; their trading value implies a fair value of CAD 1,119,655 thousand, which exceeds both figures [CP-1, debt and financing instruments]. The company says proceeds should fund capital needs through commencement of commercial production in 2027 only if the conditions precedent are met; that is management language and the conditions are not supplied [CP-1A, transaction summary; Management Language].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Other claims sit beside the notes. The Gold Stream is a derivative liability of CAD 209,286 thousand and ranks pari passu with the notes; the two royalty liabilities are CAD 78,709 thousand and CAD 136,009 thousand; lease liabilities are CAD 66,483 thousand; and the closure and reclamation provision rose to CAD 104,777 thousand from CAD 46,227 thousand at December 31, 2025 [CP-1, claims outside the debt figure]. Total liabilities of CAD 1,746,295 thousand exceed shareholders' equity of CAD 170,801 thousand. A surety bond provides reclamation security, with collateral of unstated amount; this corrects the earlier financial base statement that none was found [CP-1A, correction].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The business is concentrated in one project. Management says Eskay Creek is fully permitted and expects commercial production in 2027, but those are management statements and the retained filings still list permit challenges as a risk [CP-1A, company and operating model; Management Language]. Documented issuer behaviour is equity-funded and supportive of funding, with bought deals in February 2025 and October 2025, and no creditor-adverse action is documented; no sponsor or controlling holder is identified [CP-1A, ownership and issuer behaviour].

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Skeena has pre-funded its build: restricted cash of CAD 500,853 thousand, held for construction and interest, sits beside unrestricted cash of CAD 134,808 thousand, and both together of CAD 635,661 thousand exceed the CAD 316,513 thousand of undiscounted obligations due within one year [CP-1; Analyst Interpretation, because release of restricted funds is conditional].
